text:
Arjun Patel: Quick follow-up from today's kernel/RFC sync — I reproduced a race where paged/blocked KV eviction races with attention kernel attach and the kernel assumes contiguous KV layout. We briefly saw out-of-order KV reads and spikes in decode errors. Need to pick an approach: make kernels tolerant of fragmented pages (indirection), or enforce runtime pinning/coalescing to give kernels contiguous buffers. Opinions? :thinking:
Maya Chen: I'm leaning toward adding a small indirection layer in the kernel API: accept a vector<PageRef> + length. That avoids copies for steady-state, and we can provide a gather-copy fastpath for kernels that want contiguous memory. Pro: fewer invariants in runtime. Con: more pointer-chasing in hot loop.
Sven Eriksson: pointer chasing in attention inner loop worries me — even micro-ops matter at token-perf. Hybrid seems reasonable: fast contiguous code-path when pages are coalesced, fallback to gather-copy otherwise. We should measure fallback cost.
Lucy Park: Another option is to change eviction semantics: epoch-based pinning. When a request begins generation we pin all referenced pages (soft pin) until generation end or until a small grace period. Eviction would skip soft-pinned pages. That keeps kernel assuming contiguous ranges if runtime coalesces during pin window. Tradeoff: memory pressure + risk of pin amplification for long-running requests.
Arjun Patel: Agree with both. To make decisions pragmatic, proposal: 1) Minimal kernel API change to accept PageRef[] + residency bitmap; 2) Runtime implements coalesce-to-contiguous when possible; 3) Fallback gather-copy only when coalescing fails; 4) Implement epoch soft-pins as opt-in for heavy tail workloads.
Maya Chen: Prototype API sketch:
```
struct PageRef { u64 page_id; u32 offset; u32 len; }
attach_kv_snapshot(snapshot_id, PageRef *pages, int n_pages, bitset_t residency)
```
Kernel gets logical view, can request a contiguous buffer by asking runtime->ensure_coalesced(snapshot_id, range) which returns a pointer or NULL.
Sven Eriksson: Would like bench numbers before committing. bench-bot, can you run a small microbenchmark for gather-copy vs contiguous on A100 80GB with typical page sizes (256KB) and 2k batch?
bench-bot: ran quick compare: gather-copy fallback adds ~1.8% median latency, 3.6% p95 on the microkernel for 2k batch, page size 256KB, using memcpy-based gather. CPU cost increases ~7% under contention. (attached logs /bench/1903456789/gather-vs-copy)
notes: Action items: (1) Maya to prototype kernel API and runtime coalescer (PR by EOW). (2) Sven to run full perf matrix with mixed fragmentation. (3) Lucy to prototype epoch soft-pin and measure memory amplification. Infra: watch canaries for page-tracking regressions. Decision: lean hybrid approach (contiguous fastpath + gather-copy fallback) + optional soft-pins for edge workloads.
